core_obligations: Reduce to stalks (proof lines 16807-16812): by the stalk criterion it suffices to identify the stalks of the two sheaves at every geometric point x of X.

Compute both stalks (proof lines 16813-16825): the higher-direct-images theorem gives (h_*e^{-1}F)_x = Gamma(Spec(O^sh_{X,x}) x_X Y, e^{-1}F) and (f^{-1}g_*F)_x = (g_*F)_{f(x)} = Gamma(Spec(O^sh_{S,f(x)}) x_S T, F).

Compare (proof lines 16826-16831): the two sets are equal by applying the sections-upstairs lemma to Spec(O^sh_{X,x}) x_X Y -> Spec(O^sh_{S,f(x)}) x_S T, which is a base change of Spec(O^sh_{X,x}) -> Spec(O^sh_{S,f(x)}) because Y = X x_S T, using that this last morphism has geometrically connected fibres by hypothesis.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the identity of sheaves of sets to a comparison of geometric stalks.
Write both stalks as sections over the corresponding fibre products using the higher-direct-images theorem.
Apply sections upstairs to the base change morphism of strict henselisations, whose fibres are geometrically connected by hypothesis.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes base change for pushforwards of sheaves of sets along a flat morphism whose strict henselisations have geometrically connected fibres (statement lines 16784-16804). The proof (proof lines 16806-16831) reduces to the comparison of geometric stalks, writes both as sections over fibre products by the higher-direct-images theorem, and identifies them by sections upstairs applied to the base change of the strict henselisations. H2: one stalk computation with one application of sections upstairs.
